destination.title: Protecting accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry
destination.question: Under what model-dependent conditions can continuous or discrete gauge symmetries and extra-dimensional structure suppress unwanted PQ breaking sufficiently for the intended axion mechanism?
destination.summary: Compares protection strategies while retaining their different charge assignments, anomaly conditions, field content and breaking operators.

systems: Accidental or effective PQ sectors in gauge extensions
targets: Compatible QCD anomaly and particle content
regimes: Model-dependent effective theories and ultraviolet constructions
assumptions: Protection must be evaluated with the source's allowed operators and thresholds
Gauge origin alone does not certify the complete axion potential
conventions: Anomalous and anomaly-free gauge constructions remain distinct
excludes: Treating all gauged U(1) models as one mechanism
Automatically identifying residual discrete symmetry with discrete gauge protection

sources.title: Protecting the Axion with Local Baryon Number

evidence.text: Can gauged baryon number protect an accidental PQ symmetry from dangerous Planck-suppressed operators while its anomaly-canceling exotic fermions implement the KSVZ hidden-axion mechanism?

sources.title: High-Quality Axion Models with the Anomalous $U(1)_X$ Gauge Symmetry

evidence.text: Can an anomalous gauged U(1)X protect an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against dangerous Planck-suppressed operators using only two vector-like pairs, while permitting anomaly cancellation and approximate gauge coupling unification?

sources.title: Protecting the Axion with Local Baryon Number

evidence.text: Finds the lowest gauge-invariant scalar monomial that violates the anomalous global symmetry, then estimates its Planck-suppressed contribution to θ̄. The analysis prioritizes operators made from scalars with large VEVs.

sources.title: High-Quality Axion Models with the Anomalous $U(1)_X$ Gauge Symmetry

evidence.text: Gauge couplings are evolved numerically with two-loop RGEs and specified particle thresholds. Unification is defined by α1⁻¹ = (α2⁻¹ + α3⁻¹)/2, with mismatch Δ = |α1⁻¹ − α2⁻¹|/α1⁻¹.

sources.title: Protecting the Axion with Local Baryon Number

evidence.text: Constructs anomaly-free spectra and imposes the necessary relation Σi λi(Bi−Bi′)=0. Other anomalies further constrain the charges. Grouping charge differences into two values allows two scalar fields to generate all exotic masses.

sources.title: High-Quality Axion Models with the Anomalous $U(1)_X$ Gauge Symmetry

evidence.text: The anomaly analysis uses Ai/ki = A1X/k1X = Agravity/12 = δGS for i = 1,2,3. Non-Abelian Kac–Moody levels are positive integers; Abelian levels are positive real numbers. Other gauge anomalies are required to vanish.

sources.title: Strong-$CP$ with and without gravity

evidence.text: Does coupling QCD to gravity turn strong CP from a naturalness puzzle into a consistency condition requiring an exact axion mechanism, and can a gauge formulation protect that mechanism without a global Peccei–Quinn symmetry?

sources.title: Axion quality from the (anti)symmetric of SU($ \mathcal{N} $)

evidence.text: Can simple nonabelian gauge dynamics produce an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected against sufficiently high-dimensional UV operators, while allowing colored relics to decay and yielding viable axion and heavy-relic dark matter?

sources.title: Stabilizing the axion by discrete gauge symmetries

evidence.text: Can discrete gauge remnants protect the Peccei–Quinn axion against Planck-suppressed symmetry violation, while realizing DFSZ and KSVZ models and linking the axion scale to supersymmetry breaking and the μ term?

sources.title: Stabilizing the axion and a natural solution to the mu problem of supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can a discrete gauge symmetry protect the axion's accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against gravitational violations, while supersymmetric DFSZ dynamics relates the PQ scale to supersymmetry breaking and generates an electroweak-scale μ parameter?

sources.title: High-quality axion from exact SUSY chiral dynamics

evidence.text: Can controlled supersymmetric chiral dynamics, perturbed by anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking (AMSB), produce a QCD axion while discrete gauge symmetries suppress gravitational PQ violation?

sources.title: An extension of the SM based on effective Peccei–Quinn Symmetry

evidence.text: Can an effective Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected by a gauge symmetry address the strong CP and domain-wall problems while also organizing fermion flavor, radiative neutrino masses, dark matter and leptogenesis?

sources.title: Natural Theories of Ultralow Mass PNGB's: Axions and Quintessence

evidence.text: Can a Wilson-line PNGB remain ultralight despite Planck-scale global-symmetry breaking and provide a natural axion or quintessence field, potentially with its tiny potential generated by Planck effects themselves?

sources.title: $T′$ models with high quality flaxions

evidence.text: Can the gauged Peccei–Quinn mechanism protect a flavorful axion in a T′ flavor model against dangerous explicit PQ breaking, while retaining viable fermion textures and acceptable heavy-particle and axion phenomenology?

sources.title: Hybrid SO(10) Axion Model without Quality Problem

evidence.text: Can an anomaly-free axial gauge extension of SO(10) generate an accidental PQ symmetry sufficiently protected against Planck-suppressed breaking, while supporting axion dark matter, realistic fermion masses and distinguishable axion couplings?

sources.title: High-Quality Axions in a Class of Chiral U(1) Gauge Theories

evidence.text: Can chiral U(1) gauge theories produce accidental axions whose explicit symmetry breaking is sufficiently suppressed for quintessence, fuzzy dark matter, or a solution to the strong CP problem?

sources.title: A QCD <math display="inline"><mi>R</mi></math>-axion

evidence.text: Can an anomalous supersymmetric U(1)R serve as the Peccei–Quinn symmetry, making the R-axion the QCD axion while maintaining viable gaugino masses, tuning the cosmological constant, and protecting axion quality?

sources.title: Axionic domain wall number related to U(1)$_{\rm anom}$ global symmetry

evidence.text: Can an intermediate-scale QCD axion inherited from an anomalous string U(1) simultaneously address gravitational spoil of PQ symmetry and the cosmological domain-wall problem, despite an apparently large anomaly-related vacuum multiplicity?

sources.title: Heavy fields and the axion quality problem

evidence.text: Can intermediate heavy fields amplify gravity-induced PQ breaking enough to undermine axion-quality estimates based solely on Planck-suppressed operators, even when gauge symmetries forbid low-dimensional breaking?

sources.title: Tale of two- $U(1)$ axion models

evidence.text: How can elementary Peccei–Quinn and composite axial U(1) symmetries jointly cancel QCD and hidden-QCD CP phases, and what axion masses and photon couplings result? The axion quality problem motivates the classification.

sources.title: A natural and simple UV completion of the QCD axion model

evidence.text: Can one simple ultraviolet model explain the origin, intermediate breaking scale and high quality of Peccei–Quinn symmetry while also stabilizing its extra dimension?

sources.title: Axion models with high-scale supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Can approximately universal high-scale supersymmetry breaking accommodate a gravity-protected PQ solution, axion dark matter and gauge coupling unification, while relating the supersymmetry-breaking and PQ-breaking scales?

sources.title: Axions in a highly protected gauge symmetry model

evidence.text: Can an accidental global symmetry protected by an abelian gauge quiver yield a viable QCD axion or ultralight ALP dark matter? How are protection, the hierarchy between spontaneous-breaking and decay scales, and the colored fermions required for a QCD anomaly connected?

sources.title: Axions and a gauged Peccei-Quinn symmetry

evidence.text: Can extra-dimensional locality produce an accidental anomalous global Peccei–Quinn symmetry protected by a gauged U(1), while accommodating DFSZ or hadronic axions and correlated supersymmetry/PQ breaking scales?

sources.title: Solutions to the strong CP problem in a world with gravity

evidence.text: Which strong-CP solutions survive hypothetical Planck-scale violations of global symmetries, and can gauge symmetries protect the Peccei–Quinn mechanism sufficiently?

sources.title: Accidental Peccei-Quinn symmetry from gauged U(1) and a high quality axion

evidence.text: Can an anomaly-free gauged axial U(1)a generate accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry while suppressing gravity-induced PQ violation sufficiently to preserve the strong-CP solution and viable axion dark matter?

sources.title: Scale and quality of Peccei-Quinn symmetry and weak gravity conjectures

evidence.text: Can one hidden gauge sector simultaneously protect an accidental Peccei–Quinn symmetry against explicit breaking and explain its scale far below the Planck scale through a weak gravity conjecture? The paper also asks whether the resulting low-cutoff theory admits suitable axion cosmology.

sources.title: Tale of two- $U(1)$ axion models

evidence.text: Diagonalise anomaly-induced axion mass matrices perturbatively in the QCD contribution relative to hidden confinement, then obtain photon interactions from anomaly couplings and axion–meson mixing.

sources.title: Coloured gravitational instantons, the strong CP problem and the companion axion solution

evidence.text: Estimates the CEH collective-coordinate measure by dimensional reasoning: ρ⁻⁵dρ, normalization factors for bosonic zero modes, and one-loop running proportional to (ρΛ)^(3b/2). This is explicitly an educated guess rather than an explicit determinant calculation.

sources.title: PQ axiverse

evidence.text: For high-energy QCD instantons, lift fermion zero modes with complex dimension-six operators and a SUSY-breaking insertion, then match gauge-coupling running. For axion spectra, use Cholesky normalization and successive projections of hierarchically ordered instanton charges.

sources.title: Heavy fields and the axion quality problem

evidence.text: Use collective-breaking spurions and operator-dimension counting: several low-dimensional interactions can carry a large combined PQ charge while requiring fewer inverse Planck powers. The paper acknowledges earlier discussion of this counting for composite axions.

sources.title: Gravitational instantons and the quality problem of the QCD axion: Facts, speculations, and statements in between

evidence.text: Integrate over instanton size with a dρ/ρ5 measure, include the classical instanton weight and collective-coordinate factors, and close all fermion legs using available interactions. Split the size integral at the heavy axion-sector threshold λfa.

sources.title: Semiclassical gravity and invisible axions

evidence.text: Construct a nonlinear chiral Lagrangian with anomalous Wess–Zumino terms; integrate QCD and AEH fluctuations in a dilute-gas approximation, minimize the combined potential, and use Dashen’s theorem and mass-matrix diagonalization for the spectrum.
